provenance.description: Bundled web example (P0067); LLM-generated plan, matched to web/src/example.json.

plan.narrative: I'll finish my master's and look for a full-time job elsewhere — the simulator already moves me to full-time once I graduate, so a separate step adds nothing. I keep spending lean and only invest cash above a nine-month cushion, because my emergency fund is cash and I won't sell investments in a dip. My partner and I move in together and look for something bigger once we both earn properly. If cash gets thin I cut spending again rather than move to a cheaper place or borrow — and while I'm still studying I accept that cash may dip, because my income jumps once I graduate.

steps.label: Keep spending lean until the deposit is saved
steps.head: spending
steps.why: The CHF 40k by 2029 is tight on a student income, I keep a close eye on my savings deadline, and the simulation showed cash going negative while I studied.

steps.label: Invest cash above a nine-month buffer each January
steps.head: assets
steps.why: I save first and I'm comfortable holding investments that can lose value, but the simulation showed I need a bigger cash cushion before I invest anything.

steps.label: Cut spending further if cash runs low
steps.head: spending
steps.why: Cash dipped below zero in most simulated lives, so I want a second cut that fires before I have to borrow.

steps.label: Move to a bigger flat when my partner moves in
steps.head: housing
steps.why: We want to live together and more space is worth paying for, but only once two incomes pass the landlord's rule.

steps.label: Cut back if I lose my job
steps.head: spending
steps.why: Without a salary my cash would run down fast, and I'd rather cut spending than sell investments.

notes: Dropped the go_full_time step: it was blocked in 13% of lives and the simulator already moves me to full-time once I graduate, so the step added nothing.
Dropped the cheaper_if_short step: it was blocked in 85% of lives because a shared flat is already the cheapest home allowed; instead I protect cash by cutting spending.
Raised the investing buffer from 6 to 9 months of outgoings, because cash fell past the credit limit in half of lives, mostly in 2026 while I was still studying.
Added a second spending cut triggered by low cash, since the job-loss cut alone left 85% of lives dipping below zero.
No sell_to_buffer step: I said I'd cut spending rather than touch investments, so that stays a rule, not an action.
I stay in Zurich — the simulator can't move cities, and I don't want to.
Retirement at 65 is out of reach in this window, so no pension step.

rounds.thought: Checked the work steps: the update means the start-up won't offer full-time, so I added a full-time job search after graduation. The rest of the plan still fits.

'full_time_elsewhere' could not happen in 82% of lives when due: not possible while already full-time or already looking for full-time work, or from 70. Move its window, add a step that makes it possible, or drop it.

limitations: The saved plan is LLM-generated; its narrative and stated reasons are self-reports, not verified causal explanations.
The saved draft and revision respond to different messages and are not repeated samples of one state.
The opening intervention explains the rule policy conditioned on one state and the fixed saved plan, not the LLM; masks and triggers can change.
Exact one-step probabilities omit uncertainty about traits, state and model. Plan-step reports count different events over all paths and are not mutually exclusive.
Plan versus habits also changes spontaneity and multiple planned intentions, so it does not isolate individual steps or identify causal effects.
Financial uncertainty intervals quantify finite-path simulation error conditional on the model, not real-world forecast uncertainty.
Plan and baseline simulate same random seed, but path-dependent behaviour and events may diverge.
Saved plans revised as of a later date are simulated from January 2025; the results are counterfactual, not a reconstruction of what was known then.
All amounts nominal CHF; goal uses the simulator fixed December 2029 deadline and credit-breach rule.
The offer stress changes the simulated world with the plan fixed; it does not ask the LLM to replan.
